question.text: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the three AIF categories under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Cat I is for hedge funds; Cat II is for start-up funds; Cat III is for private equity

Cat I invests in start-ups/early-stage/social/SME/infra/special-situation/CDMDF (sectors considered socially or economically desirable by Government); Cat II funds do not fall under Cat I or III and cannot take leverage except for temporary funding (<=30 days, <=4 times/year, <=10% investable funds) — includes PE and private debt; Cat III uses diverse/complex strategies including leverage and derivatives (hedge-fund-like)
All three categories can use unlimited leverage; the distinction is tax-based
Cat I and Cat II are open-ended; Cat III is close-ended

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (pages 86-87 and 487) distinguishes the three AIF categories as follows: Category I invests in sectors considered socially or economically desirable by Government — start-ups, early-stage ventures, social ventures, SMEs, infrastructure, special situations and CDMDF; Category II covers funds that do not fall under Category I or III, such as private equity and private debt funds, and cannot take leverage other than as permitted for temporary funding requirements; Category III uses diverse or complex trading strategies, including leverage and derivatives. Pages 510 and 513-514 support the temporary funding limits applicable to Category I and II. The Trap: Option A inverts the categories. Option C is wrong because leverage is not unlimited across all categories. Option D inverts the open-ended versus close-ended treatment. Note: An AIF cannot change its category post-registration except with SEBI approval, so the category chosen at registration drives the leverage and strategy framework that applies later.
